title: Theo and the Hollow
premise: Yara Coldharbour, the palace's poison-proofed food-taster, secretly keeps the ledgers of the Guild of Impossible Things, a ragtag found family that trades in wishes, debts, and doorways. When a mute child arrives speaking a language older than any kingdom, Yara discovers the child's soul was sold to the Hollow Court beneath the mountain by a royal ancestor, and the debt comes due at midwinter. To steal it back, Yara must betray the crown she serves, trust the guild's exiled founder, and offer her own carefully hoarded immunities as collateral. In the end, Yara pays with her taste for anything sweet — a small price, she decides, for a family that finally fits.
about_author: Mirabel Yarrow is the pen name of a former archivist who spent years cataloguing medieval cookery manuscripts before turning to fantasy. She writes in a drafty attic full of mismatched teacups and insists every story should smell faintly of bread.

chapters.title: The Taster's Tongue
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. She tastes the king's supper, catalogues three poisons, then slips home to the guildhall where she balances ledgers of traded impossibilities. Establishes her double life and quiet loneliness. Emotional beat: competence as armor against belonging nowhere.

chapters.title: A Knock at Odd Hours
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. A child appears at the guild door in the rain, speaking a language no member recognizes — until the ledger itself begins translating. The guild takes the child in. Emotional beat: wary tenderness; the first crack in Yara's armor.

chapters.title: The Ledger Remembers
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Researching the child's language, Yara finds an entry from two hundred years ago: a soul sold to the Hollow Court by King Aldous I. The child is the payment, come to collect itself. Emotional beat: dread blooming into resolve.

chapters.title: Salt and Silver
chapters.summary: Bramble the hedge-witch's POV. The guild debates: return the child to the palace for reward money or honor the old trade laws and contest the sale. Bramble argues for the child. Emotional beat: found family choosing conscience over survival.

chapters.title: What the Court Owes
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. She consults the guild's exiled founder, Odile Vane, imprisoned in a lighthouse of frozen time. Odile agrees to help — for a price named later. Emotional beat: uneasy alliance; love of duty beginning to war with duty itself.

chapters.title: The Sweetness Test
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Back at the palace, Yara realizes her built-up immunities are themselves a currency the Hollow Court values. A courtier suspicious of her absences begins asking questions. Emotional beat: paranoia tightening; stakes made personal.

chapters.title: Down the Stair That Isn't There
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The party enters the mountain through a doorway only the child can open. Descent into the Hollow Court's antechambers of unlit candles and borrowed memories. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into claustrophobia.

chapters.title: The Market of Borrowed Things
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. In the Court's market, souls are shelved like preserves. They locate the child's soul-jar but learn the sale contract requires equivalent payment. Emotional beat: hope dashed by fine print.

chapters.title: The Fine Print of Kings
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile reveals she drafted the original contract — and hid a flaw inside it, a clause about willing substitution. She has waited two centuries for someone desperate enough to use it. Emotional beat: betrayal and admiration entwined.

chapters.title: Midnight in the Tasting Room
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The suspicious courtier confronts Yara; she deflects him but realizes the palace will soon mark her traitor. She chooses the guild openly in her heart. Emotional beat: the point of no return, chosen quietly.

chapters.title: The Child Speaks
chapters.summary: Child's POV (rendered impressionistically). Deep in the mountain, the child's stolen voice returns in fragments, naming what was taken: not just a soul, but a name, a mother, a winter. Emotional beat: grief given language; the guild becomes family in earnest.

chapters.title: Collateral
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Negotiations with the Hollow Regent begin. Yara offers her immunities — decades of swallowed poison — as collateral while they search for another way. Emotional beat: sacrifice offered freely, love outweighing self-preservation.

chapters.title: The Regent's Hunger
chapters.summary: Regent's POV. The Regent explains why the Court collects souls: it is starving, forgotten, kept alive only by old debts. It wants not cruelty but continuation. Emotional beat: antagonist humanized; the problem reframed.

chapters.title: An Old Debt, Reversed
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile proposes voiding the original sale by proving King Aldous stole the soul in the first place — the child was never his to sell. They need evidence from the sealed royal archive. Emotional beat: audacious plan; fragile hope.

chapters.title: Breaking the Archive
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara uses her taster's access to infiltrate the palace archive at night, nearly caught by the courtier, saved by an unlikely guard ally. She finds Aldous's confession. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into triumph.

chapters.title: The Courtier's Choice
chapters.summary: Courtier's POV. The suspicious courtier discovers Yara's treachery — and covers for her, revealing his own sister's soul was sold long ago. He joins them. Emotional beat: enemy turned brother; the family widens.

chapters.title: Midwinter Comes Early
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The Regent accelerates the debt's collection, dragging the child's soul toward consumption. The guild races back down the stair as the mountain begins to close. Emotional beat: desperation; time bleeding out.

chapters.title: The Trial Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Before the assembled Hollow Court, Odile presents Aldous's confession and invokes the flaw she planted. The Regent resists; the contract begins to unravel around them all. Emotional beat: climax of wit and nerve.

chapters.title: What Yara Swallows
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The unraveling demands a price anyway: Yara drinks the Court's final draught, surrendering her taste for sweetness forever, to seal the void and free the child. Emotional beat: sacrifice completed without hesitation.

chapters.title: The Door Closes Both Ways
chapters.summary: Regent's POV. Freed from its hunger by the honest payment, the Regent releases the Court's hoarded souls and lets the mountain sleep. The child's soul returns whole. Emotional beat: mercy as resolution; grief and grace together.

chapters.title: Sweet Nothing
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Home again, Yara faces the king's table unable to taste sugar — and finds she doesn't miss it. The guildhall smells of bread; the child has a new name. Emotional beat: belonging earned, bittersweet and warm.

chapters.title: The Next Impossible Thing
chapters.summary: Guild's collective POV. A new knock at the door, a new ledger line waiting. Yara opens it without hesitation, Odile at her shoulder, the family gathered behind. Emotional beat: the story ends where families begin — with the door held open.
